# Part V: Displays {#sec-displays .unlisted .unnumbered}
{{< include "includes/WIP-callout.qmd" >}}

**While the display chapters are being prepared, please use this review article.**

**[Characterization of Visual Stimuli using the Standard Display Model, 2024](resources/Artal-2024/Artal-2024.qmd){target=_blank}**

Joyce E. Farrell,  Haomiao Jiang, and Brian A. Wandell

Psychology and Department of Electrical Engineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305

**Key Words:**  Display technology, calibration, modeling, simulation, visual stimuli, psychophysics, pixel pointspread function, spectral power distribution

## Display topics {#sec-display-topics}

*   **Display principles (@sec-display-principles):** From light fields to planar displays, display subpixels and primary spectra, and the Standard Display Model (gamma curves, subpixel point spread functions, and linearity).
*   **Display technologies (@sec-display-technologies):** Planar and projection display mechanisms (CRTs, LCDs, OLEDs, DLPs, and MicroLEDs) alongside emerging light-field and near-eye (AR/VR) architectures, including the vergence-accommodation conflict (VAC) and passthrough latency.
*   **Display characterization (@sec-display-characterization):** Calibration measurements, testing the assumptions of the Standard Display Model (pixel independence, spectral homogeneity, and spatial uniformity / mura), and coupling ISETBio display simulations with human visual metrics (CIELAB and S-CIELAB).

## Display resources

*   **[Glossary: Displays](resources/displays-glossary.qmd):** A reference table and guide defining fundamental metrics—including luminance ($L_v$), the nit ($\text{cd/m}^2$), contrast ratio, display primaries, color gamuts (sRGB, DCI-P3, Rec. 2020), and gamma / tone reproduction curves (TRC).
*   **[Characterization of Visual Stimuli using the Standard Display Model (Artal 2024)](resources/Artal-2024/Artal-2024.qmd):** Detailed handbook chapter on computational display modeling and simulation.
